status: Curated library content; no runtime retrieval/dispatch binding installed.

entries.name: Direct molecular operation
entries.description: Represent what the target itself does: chemical transformation, binding, translocation or physical energy effect; distinguish a downstream consequence.

entries.name: Molecular target, recognition range and exact feature
entries.description: Represent which substrate, ligand, ion, macromolecule, sequence site or chemical feature is recognized or acted upon, with bounded exclusions and productive versus nonproductive recognition.

entries.name: Mode and mechanism of molecular action
entries.description: Represent how an assigned operation is physically or chemically achieved, at the level actually distinguished by evidence.

entries.name: Productive requirements and coupled reaction account
entries.description: Represent cofactors, substrates, electron/nucleotide donors and compatible partners required for productive operation, distinguishing coupled consumption from merely correlated stimulation.

entries.name: Regulatory input, target and effect
entries.description: Represent which input changes regulator state/abundance, through what route, and which target experiences activation, repression or another effect.

entries.name: Contribution within a biological system
entries.description: Represent a target’s specific responsibility in a multi-component process: execution, activation, cofactor supply, assembly, positioning, reset or another bounded contribution.

entries.name: Spatial access, export and topology
entries.description: Represent which compartment, membrane face or local site target/material can access and which export, topology or targeting feature enables the encounter.

entries.name: Native physiological contribution and its conditions
entries.description: Represent which cellular/organismal consequence an activity contributes to in biological context, preserving environmental, nutrient, temporal and population conditions.

entries.name: Conditional necessity, overlap and residual function
entries.description: Represent whether a target is needed for a named outcome under specified conditions and available alternatives: absolute loss, quantitative impairment, hidden overlap or no detected phenotype.

entries.name: Functional replacement and route equivalence
entries.description: Represent whether an alternative replaces the same reaction, one reference activity, a different route to the same product or demand for the missing function.

entries.name: Choose a relevant analogue and bound what transfers
entries.description: Use similarity to a characterized system to form bounded explanations. Choose which sequence, local structural machinery, domain architecture, genomic context or organismal circumstance makes the reference informative for the disputed property; revise misleading comparators.

entries.name: Seek cases that break a proposed predictor
entries.description: Treat an implication as something that can fail. Prefer feature/function discordance: feature without function challenges sufficiency; function without feature challenges necessity.

entries.name: Discriminate competing inputs by their predicted chemistry
entries.description: Keep the candidate system explicit while choosing substrates, co-substrates or acceptors that distinguish competing recognition hypotheses. Refine the candidate space using identified products and bounded non-products.

entries.name: Revise the failed attachment while retaining independent constraints
entries.description: After a competent negative or contradiction, separate the part of the explanation that failed from independently supported constraints. Reopen alternatives within surviving constraints without either preserving the whole annotation or discarding everything.

entries.name: Constrain missing-function hypotheses by what the system must accomplish
entries.description: Use a supported output or requirement to distinguish loss of function, unfamiliar replacement, different route and changed demand. Evaluate candidate similarities and context against these system explanations.

entries.name: Retain the system output and revise who contributes what
entries.description: Keep a real aggregate output separate from its attribution. Compare direct chemistry, substrate/cofactor supply, enabling a complex, downstream filtering and production of an observable signal.

entries.name: Distinguish restoration from bypass, compensation and reduced demand
entries.description: An improved endpoint can repair the proposed molecular relationship, use another route, reduce demand or change downstream consequences. Compare those explanations before treating rescue as mechanistic equivalence.

entries.name: Test the missing prerequisite behind conditional function
entries.description: Investigate which enabling resource or molecular state permits a supported capability to matter. Distinguish that prerequisite from correlated stress, altered protein amount and reporter failure.

entries.name: Separate physical access from chemical competence
entries.description: Explain a missing cellular reaction by contrasting inaccessible substrate/partner, absent substrate, failed catalyst and failed reporter delivery. Prefer changes that discriminate the relevant barrier.

entries.name: Account for the coupled chemical system
entries.description: Choose an explicit account of matter, electrons, cofactors and energy needed for a conversion. Reopen incomplete boundaries when an isolated reaction is implausible or replacement changes metabolic demand.

entries.name: Distinguish a possible route from the route actually used
entries.description: Keep feasibility or measured capacity separate from native use. Contrast ordinary use, conditional backup, side activity and unused capacity without forcing a single-role explanation.

entries.name: Compare biological consequences over the time that matters
entries.description: Choose time/phase contrasts distinguishing transient acceleration, repeated function, adaptation and survival. An early benefit or first product need not predict later outcomes.

entries.name: Resolve an aggregate claim at the biological level that separates explanations
entries.description: Ask whether pooled change reflects uniform effects, selective subsets or changed mixtures. Choose biologically meaningful units whose contrasts separate those explanations.

entries.name: Distinguish the transformation from its proxy readout
entries.description: Treat bands, cofactor changes, substrate loss and downstream signals as compatible with several transformations. Prefer evidence separating intended chemistry from half-reactions, spontaneous conversion or artifacts.

entries.name: Hold upstream success while investigating downstream failure
entries.description: Preserve demonstrated recognition, binding, cleavage or delivery when productive output fails. Compare the additional compatibility or coupling explanations rather than repeat upstream positives.

entries.name: Distinguish direct input action from indirect response and feedback
entries.description: Environmental responses can arise through direct ligand recognition, cofactor chemistry, changed abundance or system-demand feedback. Choose contrasts distinguishing those routes before assigning a direct sensor or regulatory sign.

entries.name: Separate linked functions through selective dissociation
entries.description: Seek comparisons preserving one property while changing another. Use their dissociation to distinguish a required functional relation from amount, delivery, stability or another linked activity.

entries.name: Reconcile conflict by testing scope-specific explanations
entries.description: Compare apparently conflicting claims without choosing a paper or averaging them. Ask whether a tested difference in organism, state, assay window, relation or construct explains disagreement; preserve unresolved conflict where no discriminating match exists.

entries.name: Investigate the route behind residual function
entries.description: Preserve reproducible output after a focal loss while distinguishing another contributor from incomplete perturbation, imported product or reduced demand. Revise exclusivity without erasing the lost route’s genuine contribution.

entries.name: Primary-source and retained-material access
entries.description: Retrieve identified publications and advertised supplements, expose exact source windows, and extract selected tables or images while preserving source identity and inspection scope.

entries.name: Protein sequence matches and local sequence features
entries.description: Retrieve exact protein sequences, compare selected homologs or database matches, and expose domain/local-residue differences without converting similarity into substrate, orthology or native-role assignments.

entries.name: Comparative gene neighborhoods, fusions and presence profiles
entries.description: Expose gene-order, strand, fusion and component-presence observations across explicitly selected genomes and proteins; count only defined records and retain unknown or incomplete context.

entries.name: Deposited structure identities, ligands and contact geometry
entries.description: Retrieve exact deposited structures and metadata, map native chains/residues/ligands, and calculate declared geometric contacts without treating a static model as activity or physiological proof.

entries.name: Fold, pocket and candidate-ligand model comparisons
entries.description: Compare supplied structures/models and candidate ligands with declared computational models; return ranked or geometric hypotheses whose tested chemical coverage is explicit.

entries.name: Reaction identities and chemical accounting
entries.description: Retrieve chemical/reaction identities and calculate explicit atom, electron, carrier and cofactor ledgers under a declared reaction boundary; leave unmeasured driving forces unknown.

entries.name: Assay-specific kinetic and signal comparisons
entries.description: Extract matched assay conditions and numeric estimates, calculate declared ratios or bounds, and expose substrate/partner and readout dependencies without relabeling apparent parameters as direct binding or native flux.

entries.name: Genotype, component and functional-perturbation tables
entries.description: Represent actual strain/construct/component contrasts and their measured outcomes, preserving the distinction between a perturbation, its validated molecular effect and the endpoint being compared.

entries.name: RNA and genomic-signal coordinate windows
entries.description: Read selected deposited signal tracks against the exact reference feature frame and calculate stated local contrasts; keep processed tracks distinct from raw-read reconstruction and transcript-processing evidence distinct from ordinary abundance.

entries.name: Mass-spectrometric identity and site-table operations
entries.description: Expose selected published product, peptide or phosphosite identifications and quantify declared table contrasts while preserving analyte/site identity, replicate structure, normalization, censoring and missingness.

entries.name: Time, population and ecological-outcome tables
entries.description: Extract outcome trajectories and condition-stratified growth, survival, reporter or competition measurements; calculate declared comparisons at the resolution actually observed.

entries.name: Regulatory DNA sites, inputs and measured-output correspondence
entries.description: Compare exact regulatory DNA sequences and mapped promoters, expose motif matches under a supplied model, and retain separate binding, molecular-input/state and transcription-output records.

entries.name: Compartment, export and membrane-access feature tables
entries.description: Expose exact sequence/topology features and source-controlled access/orientation readouts so export, processing, physical access and downstream assembly can be compared as distinct measured properties.
